reading.p: The Nicene Creed is the official statement of faith of the Church. It clearly defines what we believe about God, and especially about the Holy Trinity. We confess it together as the words that hold our faith in common.

reading.quote: We believe in one God, God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all worlds; Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made, being of one essence with the Father; by whom all things were made; Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of the Virgin Mary, and became man; And was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered and was buried; And the third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures; And ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father; And He shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end. And we believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spoke by the prophets. And in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. We acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins. We look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

reading.p: The Creed was established during two major Church councils: the First Council of Nicaea and the First Council of Constantinople. Their purpose was clear and urgent.

list: To defend the truth about Christ
To reject false teachings, such as denying Christ's divinity
To unite the Church in one clear belief

reading.p: In theology, the words "Nature" or "Essence" refer to the shared substance of God. It is what makes God to be God. There is only one Divine Nature, and it cannot be divided or shared out like a physical object.
Everything that belongs to the Godhead is possessed fully by all three Persons. They share every divine attribute completely.

list: Eternity: All three are without beginning or end.
Omnipotence: All three are Almighty; they possess all power.
Omniscience: All three know all things — past, present, and future.
Holiness: All three are the source of all holiness.

reading.p: Because they share one nature, they also share one will and one action. They act as one God with one divine will, without any confusion of the Persons.
While the Nature is one, the Persons are three. We distinguish them only by their eternal relationships to one another.

list: The Father (the Source): He is the Source, or Cause. He is Unbegotten, meaning He has no cause and comes from no one.
The Son (the Word): He is eternally Begotten of the Father. He is the Word and Wisdom of God.
The Holy Spirit (the Life-Giver): He eternally Proceeds from the Father. He is the Breath of God.

reading.p: No one Person is "more God" than the others. They are co-equal in majesty, glory, and worship. The Father is the origin within the Trinity; the Son comes from the Father by begetting; and the Holy Spirit comes from the Father by procession. This teaching is called the "Monarchy of the Father" in Orthodox theology.
To understand the Trinity, we distinguish the Persons by their "Mode of Existence." Understanding these technical terms helps us avoid heresy.

This means "Without Cause." The Father is the only Person who does not come from anyone else. He is the Source (Arche) of the Godhead. He has no source because He is the Source — He is the Mind that thinks the Thought.

This describes an Eternal Birth, not a creation. A child is "begotten" and shares the same nature as the parent, but a house is "made" and is of a different nature. The begetting of the Son is outside of time: just as a thought is born in the mind the moment the mind exists, the Son is born of the Father eternally.

This describes a Spiritual Flow. Just as breath proceeds from a person's lungs, the Spirit proceeds from the Father. We believe the Spirit proceeds only from the Father. To say He proceeds from the Son — the Filioque heresy — would suggest there are two sources in the Trinity, which we reject.
None of the Persons existed before the others. The Father was never without His Word (the Son) or His Breath (the Spirit). These are eternal relationships, not events in time.

There is a great difference between human begetting and the divine begetting of the Son. A human is begotten in time, has a beginning, is a created being, and possesses human nature. The Son is begotten eternally, has no beginning, is not created, and possesses the divine nature.

list: The Son is begotten of the Father eternally.
He did not begin to exist.
He is fully God, with the same divine nature as the Father.
The Son is begotten outside of time.

reading.p: Think of a mountain spring. The water is simply there. It did not flow from another pipe or another mountain; it is the Source. In plain English, "Unbegotten" means the Father is the Start. He does not have a source because He is the source.

reading.h3: Begotten — The Thought and the Word

reading.p: Think of a thought in your mind. The moment you have a thought, it is "born" in your head; it did not take time to grow, but appeared because you are a thinking being. "Begotten" means the Son comes from the Father like a word comes from a thought. A word has the same "stuff" as the thought — if you think of an apple, your word is "apple," and they are of the same nature. The Son is the Word of God, meaning He is exactly like the Father.

reading.h3: Proceeding — The Breath that Carries the Word

reading.p: Think of your breath. When you speak a word, your breath carries that word out into the room. You do not give birth to your breath like a baby; it flows out of you. "Proceeding" means the Spirit flows from the Father like breath or energy. We use a different word because the Spirit relates to the Father differently than the Son does: if the Son is the Word God speaks, the Spirit is the Life and Breath that makes the Word alive.

reading.h2: The Father as Source — Without Inequality

reading.p: "Unbegotten" means the Father does not come from anyone else: He is not born from another, not made by another, not caused by another, not created by another. The Father has no source because He is the Source. This does not mean the Father existed before the Son or before the Holy Spirit — God is not trapped inside time as we are.

The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are all eternal. There was never a time when the Father was without His Son or without His Spirit. When we say the Father is "the Source," we are not saying He is greater in nature; we are saying this is what makes Him personally the Father.

list: The Father is fully God.
The Son is fully God.
The Holy Spirit is fully God.

reading.p: The difference is not in their divinity. The difference is in their personal relationship to one another.

reading.h2: The Son — Birth of the Word

reading.p: When you speak a word, that word comes from inside you. It is not something outside that you built with your hands; it comes from your mind and expresses what is already in you. So when we call Jesus the Word of God, we mean the Son perfectly reveals who the Father is. He is not a separate kind of being and is not less than the Father. He is from the Father and shares the same divine nature, and that is why He is fully God, just as the Father is fully God.

We must hold the difference between making and begetting clearly. To make is to create something different from yourself: a carpenter makes a table, but the table is wood and the carpenter is human, and they do not share the same nature. To beget is to produce something exactly the same as yourself: a human begets a human, and a lion begets a lion. So God made the stars, but He begat the Son — the stars are not God, but the Son is.

This begetting is eternal. Think of light coming from a flame: the light is "born" from the flame, yet both begin at the exact same time. There was never a flame without its light. The Son is the Father's perfect Self-Expression; everything the Father is, the Son is — except that He is the Son and not the Father.

"Proceeding" describes the Holy Spirit's eternal relationship to the Father. The Holy Spirit is not created, not made, and not begotten like the Son. He eternally proceeds from the Father, flowing from Him like breath or energy.

This does not mean the Holy Spirit is merely air, energy, or an impersonal force. He is a divine Person — fully God, eternal, and one in essence with the Father and the Son. The Son is begotten from the Father; the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father. These are not two ways of being created, but two eternal relationships within the Holy Trinity. The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father, gives life, and is worshipped together with the Father and the Son as one God.
These three terms identify the eternal personal distinctions in the Trinity. They tell us who each Person is, not what kind of nature each one has.

list: The Father alone is unbegotten — this distinguishes the Father.
The Son is eternally begotten of the Father — this distinguishes the Son.
The Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father — this distinguishes the Holy Spirit.

reading.p: The Son and the Spirit are both fully God and both from the Father, but they are not the same Person, because their origin from the Father is not identical: the Son is from the Father by begetting, and the Spirit is from the Father by procession. The Church confesses this distinction but does not reduce it to biology, mechanics, or material imagery.

reading.h2: The Two Hands of God — Creation

reading.p: In the teaching of the Church Fathers, especially St. Irenaeus, the Son and the Holy Spirit are called the "Two Hands" of the Father. This teaches that the one God creates and acts through His Word and His Spirit.

reading.quote: By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made… and all the host of them by the Breath of His mouth.
Then the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made.

reading.p: The Father creates through His Word (the Son) and gives life through His Breath (the Holy Spirit). This image helps us understand God's work, but it does not fully explain the mystery of the Trinity.

The same "Hands" that created us are the same "Hands" that save us. Just as God used His Word and Breath to create Adam, He used them to restore humanity. In the Incarnation, the Father wills the salvation of the world, the Holy Spirit (the Breath/Hand) descends upon the Virgin Mary, and the Son (the Word/Hand) takes on human flesh.
There is no separation in this work. In every act of God — from creating the stars to the birth of Christ — all three Persons are present and active as One.

reading.h2: The Relevance of the Number Three

reading.p: These examples are not comparisons to the Trinity itself, but they show how the number three is woven through creation. From science and biology to mathematics and structure, threes appear all around us.

list: The Atom: built from protons, neutrons, and electrons.
Space: defined by length, width, and height.
Time: experienced as past, present, and future — three distinct "times" in one timeline.
Primary colors of light: red, green, and blue.
The Triple Point of Water: a specific temperature and pressure where water exists as solid, liquid, and gas at once.
The Human Person: traditionally described as body, soul, and spirit (or mind), yet one whole person.
DNA: written in codons, groups of three chemical bases.
The Family Unit: father, mother, and child.
The Triangle: the most stable shape in engineering — three sides and three angles, yet one object.
The Musical Triad: the most fundamental chord, three notes played together.
Navigation: GPS uses trilateration, requiring signals from at least three satellites to find one point.

reading.p: The Church Fathers use the image of fire to help us visualize the Trinity without dividing the Godhead. The flame is the source and represents the Father as the Root or Cause. As soon as the candle is lit, light is born (begotten) from the flame — you cannot have the flame without the light, and this represents the Son. The heat comes forth (proceeds) from the flame; it is distinct from the light yet inseparable from the flame, and this represents the Holy Spirit.

list: Unity: they are one single fire.
Simultaneity: the light and heat do not wait to appear — they exist as soon as the flame exists, which is co-eternity.

reading.p: This is only an analogy. God is beyond all comparison.

reading.h2: Scriptural Witness — The Baptism in the Jordan

reading.p: At the Jordan River, the Trinity was physically manifested. The Father's voice spoke from the heavens: "This is My beloved Son." The Son was physically present in the water, being baptized as a man. The Holy Spirit descended from heaven in the form of a dove.

Christ also commanded us to baptize in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Notice that He said "Name," singular — not "Names." The one Name reveals one God in three Persons, the Godhead.

reading.quote: ...baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

reading.p: The Father is not the Son, and the Son is not the Spirit. We do not mix the Persons together, and so we reject Modalism — the Trinity is unified without confusion. At the same time, the Persons are never apart: where one is, the others are also, and so we reject Tritheism — the Trinity is distinguished without separation.
We do not master this mystery with logic. We enter into it through prayer and the Sacraments, and we offer it our worship.

reading.quote: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

studyGuide.overview: This lesson teaches the Holy Trinity as the Church confesses it in the Nicene Creed: one God in one Divine Nature (essence), existing as three distinct Persons. The Father is the unbegotten Source, the Son is eternally begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father, all co-equal and co-eternal as one God.
keyPoints: There is one Divine Nature (essence) shared fully and equally by all three Persons.
The three Persons are distinguished only by their eternal relationships: Unbegotten (Father), Begotten (Son), Proceeds (Holy Spirit).
Begetting is an eternal birth, not a creation; the Son is of the same nature as the Father, not made.
The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father alone; the Filioque (procession from the Son) is rejected.
The 'Monarchy of the Father' means the Father is the personal Source within the Trinity, not greater in nature.
The Son and Spirit are the 'Two Hands' of the Father in both creation and salvation.
The Trinity is unified without confusion (against Modalism) and distinguished without separation (against Tritheism).
reviewQuestions: Which two councils established the Nicene Creed, and what was their purpose?
What is the difference between 'Nature/Essence' and 'Person' in the Trinity?
Explain the difference between 'begetting' and 'making.' Why does it matter for the Son?
From whom does the Holy Spirit proceed, and why does the Church reject the Filioque?
What does the 'Monarchy of the Father' mean, and does it make the Father greater than the Son or Spirit?
How are the Son and Spirit the 'Two Hands' of the Father in creation and in the Incarnation?
How does the Baptism in the Jordan reveal the Trinity, and why is the singular 'Name' in Matthew 28:19 important?

checks: Trinity: one essence, three co-equal and co-eternal Persons — affirmed
Nicene Creed and first councils (Nicaea, Constantinople) upheld
Son eternally begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father — affirmed
Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father alone; Filioque explicitly named as heresy and rejected
Monarchy of the Father stated without subordinating Son or Spirit in nature
Holy Spirit confessed as a divine Person, fully God, not a mere force
Theotokos (Virgin Mary) referenced in the Incarnation per the Creed
